summary: Operator blocker text is produced when runtime has a receipt but no parseable AgentFramework observation summary for that exact step.

evidence.note: BuildOperatorProblemSummary appends “No AgentFramework result summary was found…” when receipt exists but diagnostic is null.
Diagnostic is null when there is no observation, no raw ResultSummary, no last error and no failed tool receipts.

root_cause: The UI hint hides the real failure when the observation reader misses the step run or ResultSummary is empty. This turns concrete process failures into blind rework loops.
fix: Query observations by exact (ProcessRunId, StepInstanceId), persist structured final output into ResultSummary, and fall back to StrategyResultReceipt diagnostics when AgentFramework observation is unavailable.

summary: Observation reader takes N latest records per process run, not per step; a blocker step can disappear from diagnostics in larger/nested processes.

evidence.note: Query contains RunIds, FromUtc, ToUtc, TakePerRun only; no step filter.
Execution runs are grouped by ProcessRunId and TakePerRun is applied before exact step matching.
ListExecutionRunsAsync queries by ProcessRunId only; ProcessStepId is not supplied.

root_cause: For multi-team processes, there can be many AgentFramework runs in one process run. The UI later groups by step, but the needed step may already have been truncated.
fix: Extend ProcessExecutionObservationQuery with StepInstanceIds or StepSelectors and query ExecutionRunQuery with ProcessStepId where possible. Use run-level fallback only for live dashboards, not for operator actions.

summary: Parent subprocess step has two competing orchestration models: runtime-coordinated launch and template/agent-owned launch via project_structure_process_subprocess_launch.

evidence.note: Adapter can launch a mapped subprocess before agent execution and can return a deferred/result outcome.
Step doc tells the agent to launch subprocess with the governed tool and submit ParentDeferredOutcomeJson exactly.
Runtime can build a completed parent outcome from child evidence refs.

root_cause: When runtime and agent both think they own subprocess coordination, the same step can be completed, deferred, blocked, or retried through inconsistent routes. Rework repeats because the control-plane decision is not deterministic.
fix: Make subprocess launch/wait/handoff runtime-owned. Keep the tool only as a compatibility/manual path. Do not ask normal agents to launch controlled child processes for StepKind=Subprocess.

summary: Completed child runs are mapped to parent evidence by generic child assignment refs, not by validated accepted child output contract.

evidence.note: ResolveCompletedChildEvidenceRefs adds every existing child step artifact under the child run, or the child steps folder fallback.
Parent expected output maps only to SubprocessChildStepKey setup-handoff and title Setup handoff packet.
Text says setup-handoff-after-repair is also accepted, but this is not represented as a machine-readable accepted output array.

root_cause: The parent required slot solution-skeleton-evidence is not deterministically written from the accepted child handoff packet. A product skeleton may exist while the process contract still has no accepted parent artifact.
fix: Introduce ParentSubprocessArtifactBridge that validates child terminal branch/step/artifact and writes a parent managed artifact for the exact parent produced slot.

summary: Runtime enforces missing output/input contracts into NeedsManager, but artifact ledger events are built from the original command result.

evidence.note: appliedResult is produced by EnforceStepFinalizationContract and used for status/receipts/slots.
BuildArtifactLedgerEvents receives command, not appliedResult.
BuildArtifactLedgerEvents uses command.Result.ProducedArtifacts.

root_cause: If finalization downgrades a success to NeedsManager, the artifact ledger may still reflect original produced artifacts instead of the applied result. This can corrupt later availability/diagnostics.
fix: Change BuildArtifactLedgerEvents to take StrategyResultEnvelope appliedResult and only write ledger events for the applied produced artifacts and completed/evidence-valid result policy.

summary: The runtime step contract exposed to agents contains mostly GUID slot IDs and hashes, not semantic artifact titles, keys, refs, or child mapping.

evidence.note: RequiredArtifactInputRef and ExpectedProducedArtifactRef are minimal and slot-id centric.
Prompt lists slot GUIDs, producer IDs, artifact IDs and hashes; output artifacts are only slot IDs.

root_cause: For an LLM agent, “write 1 required artifact slot” is not actionable. It needs the artifact expectation key/title, managed write ref, accepted source refs, and exact completion gate.
fix: Add semantic artifact slot descriptors and render them into prompts, diagnostics, operator hints and rework packets.

summary: Adapter result conversion synthesizes produced artifacts with a new ArtifactInstanceId and a hash derived from raw output, not from the managed artifact content.

evidence.note: ProducedArtifactRef uses ArtifactInstanceId.New() and ComputeHash(rawOutputHash:stepId:slotId).
Runtime can synthesize a primary markdown artifact when no write receipt exists.

root_cause: Downstream steps see slot availability, but the artifact identity/hash does not necessarily represent the actual managed file content. This weakens recovery and reproducibility.
fix: Tie produced artifact refs to deterministic managed artifact IDs and content hashes after materialization/readback. Store primary managed ref in the artifact receipt.

summary: Readiness checks infer project-structure tool availability from agent config/access, but do not prove the exact runtime tool is composed and authorized for the governed process context.

evidence.note: Project structure tool readiness checks read/write flags and known tool name classification.
Actual tool execution requires scoped process write access and can throw ProcessSubprocessLaunchDenied.
Scoped access depends on GovernedProcessAutomation, audit scope, process run/step IDs and allowed operations.

root_cause: A step can be claimed by an apparently suitable agent, but fail at execution because the actual runtime provider/tool was not composed for the current context.
fix: Add exact composed-tool preflight before claim/dispatch. If required tool missing, block with a concrete runtime diagnostic before invoking the agent.

summary: prepare-solution-skeleton has manual skip enabled and accepted child outputs are partly prose-only.

evidence.note: StepKind Subprocess; SubprocessProcessKey dotnet-solution-setup; AllowsManualSkip true; accepted repair handoff appears only in prose.

root_cause: The runtime cannot distinguish “already-existing skeleton proof” from skipped/missing child evidence unless this is a typed branch/output contract.
fix: Disable manual skip for this step or require an explicit AlreadyExistingSkeletonProof output contract. Add SubprocessContract with accepted and no-go child outputs.

summary: Manager rework appends a generic instruction that often cannot change the root condition.

evidence.note: Recovery instruction is generic and primarily lists diagnostics/requested artifact slot IDs.
Operator instruction says to preserve artifacts and produce required evidence, but lacks exact bridge/tool/action context when diagnostic is missing.

root_cause: Rework repeats the same hidden tool/artifact/subprocess mismatch. A manager instruction should include the actual execution run, failed tool receipt, child run state, managed refs and exact next action.
fix: Create a BlockedStepPacket and include it in operator action and rework prompt. Do not allow blind retry when diagnostic is missing.

summary: Many step Notes fields are long, imperative and tool-specific. Critical gates are hidden in prose instead of typed policy.

evidence.note: Scaffold/test/validation rules are long textual instructions, although some hard gates exist as launch variables or capability receipts.

root_cause: LLM agents miss one hard gate in long prose, then finalization blocks them. The runtime cannot reliably validate prose-only requirements.
fix: Move hard gates to typed CompletionGates, RequiredReceipts, RequiredPaths, RequiredFileContentChecks, BranchRules and SubprocessContracts. Keep prose short as explanatory guidance.

summary: Several process/MAF classes are very large and mix orchestration, policy, projection, diagnostics and UI support concerns.

evidence.note: Large policy class.
Projection, diagnostics, operator messages, enrichment and action composition are coupled.
Adapter conversion, validation and issue construction are coupled.

root_cause: Behavior is hard to reason about, so fixes are added as more guards/prose instead of small contracts and deterministic services.
fix: During these fixes split by responsibility: observation correlation, blocked packet builder, artifact descriptor resolver, parent subprocess bridge, completion gate validator, result summary persistence.
